WARRICK COUNTY RECORDER
The Warrick County Recorder is responsible for maintaining records related to real property in the county. This includes recording and storing documents such as deeds, mortgages, liens, and other documents that affect the ownership and legal status of real property. The recorder's office may also be responsible for issuing marriage licenses, maintaining records of births, deaths, and other vital events, and issuing various permits and licenses. The goal of the recorder's office is to provide accurate and up-to-date information on real property in the county.
STAFF AND MEMBERS
Recorder
Patricia E. Perry
Resources
County Recorder's Office
Records Deeds, Mortgages, Assignments, Releases, Real Estate Contracts, Power of Attorneys, Planned Developments, Plats, Surveys, Affidavits, Articles of Incorporation, Bonds, Federal Tax Liens, Mechanic Liens, Sewer Liens, Assumed Business Names, and Other Miscellaneous documents submitted for recording, providing it meets essential requirements (*see below, click on Recorder’s Fees)
File Uniform Commercial Code instruments
Provide copies and certified copies of documents upon request (Fee charged)
Military Discharges (NO CHARGE)
All recorded documents are public record and copies are available at our office or online. There is a nominal fee of $1.00 per page for copies. We accept cash, check or credit card for payments of copies and recording documents. You may also contact our office, pay for the copy online using a credit or debit card and we will gladly fax or e-mail the copy to you. Please visit our Quick Links below to learn more about the additional cost involved using a credit card.
Office hours: 8:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. Monday through Friday
“Same Day Recording” cutoff time is 2:30 p.m.
After 2:30 p.m. the Recorded Date will be the following day.
The Judicial Center is closed holidays and weekends.
Before recording deeds, contract purchases, easements or plats, the documents first must be approved and stamped by both the Assessor and Auditor.
Legally We Can Not
Answer any legal questions, such as “how do I complete” any document – you will need to contact an attorney to assist you further.
Notarize any forms.
We do not provide or have blank legal documents or forms with the exception of the “Assumed Business Name” certificate. For more information about said certificate, please visit the Secretary of State by following this link Secretary of State, Business Division.
We cannot prepare, draft, or complete legal documents.
